evidence.quote: The vast majority of nose bleeds occur in the anterior ( front ) part of the nose from the nasal septum . This area is richly endowed with blood vessels ( Kiesselbach 's plexus ) .
Bleeding farther back in the nose is known as a posterior bleed and is usually due to bleeding from Woodruff 's plexus , a venous plexus situated in the posterior part of inferior meatus .

Sometimes blood flowing from other sources of bleeding passes through the nasal cavity and exits the nostrils . It is thus blood coming from the nose but is not a true nosebleed , that is , not truly originating from the nasal cavity . Such bleeding is called pseudoepistaxis ( pseudo + epistaxis ) .
